recognize_zh: 低倍周邊血中散佈多個細長、兩端尖的鐮刀狀紅血球（sickle cells），並有標示的有核紅血球（NRBC）與後髓細胞（metamyelocyte），白血球明顯增多，符合鐮刀型貧血危象時的骨髓應激反應。
features: Scattered elongated, crescent-shaped sickle cells with pointed ends throughout the field
Circulating nucleated red blood cells with small dense nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm (labeled)
Increased leukocytes, mostly segmented neutrophils, with a left shift including a metamyelocyte (labeled)
Background anisopoikilocytosis with occasional target cells
Scattered small dark blue particles consistent with platelets and/or stain precipitate
describe_en: Low-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows leukocytosis composed predominantly of segmented neutrophils with a left shift, including a metamyelocyte. Numerous circulating nucleated red blood cells are present. Red cells show anisopoikilocytosis with scattered irreversibly sickled cells and occasional target cells. Findings are consistent with sickle cell disease with nucleated red cells and a leukoerythroblastic-type stress response, as seen in sickle cell crisis.

ddx.vs: HbSC shows fewer classic sickle cells and more target cells, folded cells and blunt-ended crystalline HbC-SC forms; hemoglobin electrophoresis/HPLC separates them.
Marrow infiltration or myelofibrosis shows NRBC and immature granulocytes with teardrop cells rather than sickle cells.
Elliptocytes are oval with blunt rounded ends and uniform hemoglobin, whereas sickle cells are crescentic with pointed ends.
Lymphocytes have a thin rim of pale blue cytoplasm, whereas NRBC have round pyknotic nuclei within pink to polychromatic hemoglobinized cytoplasm.
